name: Deep Learning 10 — Practice Lab (Class Activation Maps and Image Regression)
description: Guided learner workspace for the tenth lab of a Deep Learning course (v1.0, run in Google Colab or local Jupyter) on how much of a CNN class score can be attributed to parts of an image, and how large an image-regression model's error is. On the Inno Agent side an explanatory tutor works: the learner runs the complete cells of their own notebook one at a time (PTE_DL10_MAGYARAZHATOSAG.ipynb, 28 points in the order fixed by the cell map: E01 environment, GPU gate and division of work, K01 discussion on class versus number, C01–C02 the two new sample images and the reference preprocessing helper, C03 logits, softmax and the top-5 list, C04 the feature map and its weighted sum, C05 the classic CAM with the logit check, C06 two target classes on one shared scale, C07 a fixed occlusion experiment, C08 discussion on what a heat map does not prove, A01–A05 the age data download with checksum, data checks and distribution, the supplied age-group-stratified 60/20/20 split helper, the data streams with one full batch and the single consistent preprocessing step, B01–B02 the meaning of MAE and an image-free median baseline, F01–F02 the frozen ResNet50 feature extractor and the ordered, version-bound feature cache, M01–M03 a single-output linear head with 2049 trainable parameters, its training with early stopping, and the separate measurement after restoring the best val_mae checkpoint, V01–V03 the final test with per-image errors, per-group error counts with signed means and real large/small-error samples, X01 the regression contribution map, and Z01–Z02 three closing connections plus the learner's own summary). Three points are discussion only (K01, C08, Z01); the other 25 are code cells. The detailed lesson script holds the complete code and the interpretation questions, the concept guide supplies the conceptual support and a fallback path, the source notes record the data version and the public sources, and assets/ carries the two sample images with the public ImageNet class index. The learner writes no code and is never asked for the notebook, a submission, a share link or a saved artifact; no homework and no extra task.
